copyright: Standing stones at Avebury in Wiltshire, England (© George W Johnson/Getty Images)
description: As morning mist drifts among the standing stones of Avebury in Wiltshire, England, the scene feels almost timeless. These ancient megaliths form part of one of the world's most remarkable prehistoric landscapes, centred on a vast Neolithic monument built around 4,500 years ago. Avebury contains the world's largest prehistoric stone circle, as well as a massive henge and stone avenues extending into the surrounding countryside. Together with nearby monuments such as Silbury Hill and West Kennet Avenue, it forms part of an extensive Neolithic complex that has fascinated generations of visitors, researchers and archaeologists.

copyright: Kunětická hora Castle, Bohemia, Czechia (© Marek Saroch/Alamy)
description: What stories could these walls tell? Rising above eastern Bohemia in Czechia, Kunětická hora Castle has witnessed centuries of history. Dating to the late 14th century, the castle gradually evolved into an impressive fortress and noble residence. Its elevated position offered commanding views of the surrounding countryside and helped make it an important stronghold.

copyright: A grove of pond cypress trees with autumn foliage, Georgia, United States (© Chris Moore/Getty Images)
description: Reflected in calm water and glowing in the light of the setting sun, this grove of pond cypress creates a striking display of colour and symmetry. Native to the south-eastern United States, the species is associated with shallow ponds, depressions and wetland habitats. This image was captured in Georgia, where these trees can be found in places such as the Okefenokee Swamp and other low-lying wetlands.

copyright: Autumn waterfalls near Sitovo, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria (© Nadya85/Getty Images)
description: In Bulgaria's Western Rhodope Mountains, autumn leaves gather beside the rushing waters of Sitovo Waterfall. Near the village of Sitovo, southwest of Plovdiv, the falls tumble beneath an old stone bridge whose arch frames the cascades like a storybook scene. Moss-covered stones and pine trees add shades of green to the autumn landscape, while fallen leaves gather along the water's edge or drift through its pools. The falls become especially lively after rain and during spring snowmelt, when the surrounding woodland echoes with the sound of rushing water.

copyright: Maligne Lake, Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada (© Andrey Popov/Getty Images)
description: When night falls in Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada, the mountains get a whole new backdrop. Designated a Dark-Sky Preserve in 2011, the park spans more than 11,000 square kilometres, with measures in place to reduce light pollution. Here, the stars, planets and the Milky Way put up a celestial show, giving visitors a reason to look up. Then morning arrives and the focus shifts from the sky above to the landscape below.

copyright: Green-headed tanager (© Juan Carlos Vindas/Getty Images)
description: In much of Brazil, July is synonymous with cold weather, mist and muted tones. The green-headed tanager goes in the opposite direction. Green, blue, turquoise, yellow, black, orange and touches of violet come together on a body just over 13 centimetres long, appearing among the branches like a living argument for extravagance. It is no surprise that it frequently features on lists of the most beautiful birds in the world.

copyright: Two grey wolves, Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, United States (© John Morrison/Getty Images)
description: Two grey wolves move through the sagebrush of Yellowstone National Park in Wyoming, home to some of North America's most closely watched wolf packs. Their thick coats help them withstand harsh winters, and their keen senses make them skilled hunters and communicators.
